t: This is the site of the London School of Medicine for Women, founded in 1874 as the first medical school in Britain to train women as doctors. Three pioneers are linked to its founding. Elizabeth Blackwell was the first woman to earn a medical degree in the United States. Elizabeth Garrett Anderson was the first woman to qualify in Britain as a physician and surgeon, and served as the school's dean. Sophia Jex-Blake campaigned for women's access to medical education and helped found medical schools for women in both London and Edinburgh.
